# Definition of Done

*Generated from `validate_done.py`. Edit the source, not this file.*

| # | A task is done when… |
|---|---|
| `DOD-001` | Evidence is recorded, and every evidence reference resolves |
| `DOD-002` | Every linked requirement is both implemented and verified in the graph |
| `DOD-003` | Every linked acceptance criterion has a scenario executing it |
| `DOD-004` | A `risk-mitigation` task has reduced its risk, with evidence on the risk |
| `DOD-005` | No edge touching the node is marked `broken` |
| `DOD-006` | A `test` task names acceptance criteria, and each one is registered |

s29 asks for `status: done` to be *a computed governance state rather than a casual AI declaration*. These are the computations:

```bash
python3 .specify/extensions/openup/scripts/python/validate_done.py --json
```

Two of s29's clauses are missing on purpose. Contract tests and Microcks conformance have nothing behind them yet (see the project README's Limitations), and a check that cannot fail is worse than a missing one — it reports compliance it never established.

A node marked `done` that fails any row above is not done. Carrying work into the next iteration is normal; a green board that does not match the repository is not.
